name: Optical Bloom Artifact Analysis
description: Examines intensity spillover around high-contrast light sources. Generative AI models often synthesize artificial 'bloom' and light-bleed effects that lack the physically accurate point spread function (PSF) and exponential decay characteristics produced by real camera lenses.
algorithm: Luminance Thresholding and Exponential Decay Modeling
mechanism: Isolates overexposed regions (luminance > threshold) and analyzes the surrounding gradient of light diffusion (the point spread function). In physical photography, bloom follows a predictable exponential decay pattern caused by glass imperfect scattering and sensor bleeding. AI models usually simply 'paint' these halos as flat gradients that fail standard physical scattering models, yielding anomalous decay rates and unnatural color channel clipping.
parameters: Luminance Threshold: > 95%, Spatial Metric: Radial exponential decay rate, Feature: Point Spread Function (PSF) anomaly
accuracy: Moderate (65-75%) - Highly effective for night scenes or highly illuminated synthetic images.
source: Farid (2009) on illumination and optical physics forensics
useCase: Detecting synthetic light sources, identifying fake specular highlights, and spotting digitally overlaid visual effects in high-contrast scenes.

references.title: Farid, H. (2009). Image Forgery Detection. IEEE Signal Processing Magazine.
Wang, S.Y. et al. (2020). CNN-generated images are surprisingly easy to spot. CVPR.

strengths:
• Deeply tied to the physical limits of optical sensors and glass lenses.
• Provides highly interpretable data regarding lighting and scene consistency.
• Does not heavily rely on deep learning classifiers for optical anomaly detection.
• Especially sensitive to synthetic digital art and excessive amateur post-processing.
limitations:
• Ineffective on flat-lit images lacking bright highlights or visible light sources.
• High-end CGI rendering engines with raytracing can simulate physically accurate bloom.
• Extreme HDR tonemapping can alter natural decay curves, causing false positives.
• Highly susceptible to errors if the image was captured through dirty, wet, or smeared lenses.
